import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 288

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/288](https://www.erdosproblems.com/288)
-/

namespace Erdos288

/--
Is it true that there are only finitely many pairs of intervals $I_1$, $I_2$ such that
$$
\sum_{n_1 \in I_1} \frac{1}{n_1} + \sum_{n_2 \in I_2} \frac{1}{n_2} \in \mathbb{N}?
$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288 : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Finite { I : Fin 2 → ℕ+ × ℕ+ |
    ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧
      ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin 2, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n } := by
  sorry

/--
This is still open even if $|I_2| = 1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288.variants.i2_card_eq_1 : answer(sorry) ↔ Set.Finite { (I, n₂) : (ℕ+ × ℕ+) × ℕ+ |
    I.1 ≤ I.2 ∧ ∃ n : ℕ+, ∑ n₁ ∈ Set.Icc I.1 I.2, (n₁⁻¹ : ℚ) + (n₂⁻¹ : ℚ) = n } := by
  sorry

/--
It is perhaps true with two intervals replaced by any $k$ intervals.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288.variants.k_intervals : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ k, Set.Finite { I : Fin k → ℕ+ × ℕ+ |
    ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧
      ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin k, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n } := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true for any $k > 2$ that only finitely many $k$ intervals satisfy this condition?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_288.variants.exists_k_gt_2 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ k > 2, Set.Finite { I : Fin k → ℕ+ × ℕ+ |
      ∀ j, (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧
        ∃ n : ℕ+, (∑ j : Fin k, ∑ nⱼ ∈ Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2, (nⱼ⁻¹ : ℚ)) = n } := by
  sorry

end Erdos288

reformulations.difference: Represents intervals by valid positive endpoint pairs, and places the positive-integer witness for the total sum inside the per-interval universal quantifier.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Nonempty finite intervals of positive integers have unique minimum and maximum endpoints, so this encoding preserves finiteness. The total sum is independent of the outer index j; since Fin 2 is inhabited, requiring its integrality for every j is equivalent to requiring it once alongside all endpoint bounds. The sum is strictly positive, so a natural-number value is necessarily a positive natural. The corresponding membership and finiteness equivalences were proved in the scratch file, including exact_main_rhs_iff.

reformulations.difference: Replaces the second interval and its cardinality-one condition with its unique element n₂.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A nonempty closed interval has cardinality one exactly when its endpoints coincide, and its reciprocal sum is then 1/n₂. This gives a bijective parameterization preserving finiteness, proved as singleton_finiteness_iff. Also verified that Lean parses the displayed addition outside the sum: the expression is (∑ n₁ ∈ I₁, 1/n₁) + 1/n₂, not a sum containing repeated copies of 1/n₂. The source's [3,6], n₂=20 example evaluates to 1.

reformulations.difference: Quantifies over all natural k, including zero, and repeats the integrality condition under ∀ j : Fin k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For positive k, the repeated condition is equivalent to one common integrality condition, and positivity justifies the positive-natural target. At k=0 the universal condition is vacuous, but there is exactly one function from Fin 0, so its solution set is finite. Thus this additional case does not change the conjecture for each positive k. Proved all_k_iff_positive_k and the underlying set-membership equivalences.

review.notes: Checked all four declarations. The final exists_k_gt_2 statement is the weaker subquestion asking whether some k>2 works, not another formulation of the universal k_intervals conjecture. Padding a solution tuple with [1,1] preserves integrality and is injective, so its RHS is equivalent to finiteness for k=3; this was proved as some_higher_iff_three. The cited website still records the problem and singleton variant as open, with no accepted resolution indicated for the higher-interval questions. All experiments are in /workspace/review/; scratch.lean compiles successfully, and the equivalence proofs' axiom lists contain no sorryAx. No repository files were edited.
